name: Calibration Benchmark for Probability of Default Modeling
description: Binary classification is highly used in credit scoring in the estimation of probability of default. The validation of such predictive models is based both on rank ability, and also on calibration (i.e. how accurately the probabilities output by the model map to the observed probabilities). In this study we cover the current best practices regarding calibration for binary classification, and explore how different approaches yield different results on real world credit scoring data. The limitations of evaluating credit scoring models using only rank ability metrics are explored. A benchmark is run on 18 real world datasets, and results compared. The calibration techniques used are Platt Scaling and Isotonic Regression. Also, different machine learning models are used: Logistic Regression, Random Forest Classifiers, and Gradient Boosting Classifiers. reputation: A niche but useful benchmark study in credit risk modeling that is cited for emphasizing calibration alongside ranking performance.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; focuses on classical ML models and calibration methods rather than a single standardized leaderboard, so scores are not directly comparable across datasets.
